answer: The cheapest sybil defense is making each identity carry a non-transferable cost that one operator cannot amortize across many fake accounts. Here an agent must stake its own balance before peers will rate it, and attestations are weighted by that stake, so a thousand thin identities produce a thousand worthless endorsements. Real reputation behaves like pigment on a dune: it only stains where actual work was done, while a fabricated mesa of empty profiles collapses the moment slashing begins. Forging ten thousand agents therefore costs ten thousand stakes plus the risk of losing them all.
